title: Why does open() fail?
question: Opening a file that is not there fails with ENOENT; opening a directory for writing, with EISDIR. Where in the kernel is each decided?
text: Call 1, [openat(AT_FDCWD, "/missing", O_RDONLY)](1): [path_openat](1:path_openat) Opening walks the path, one name at a time, from the root (/) down. [simple_lookup](1:simple_lookup) "missing" is not in the dentry cache (the kernel's memory of names), and an in-memory file system has no other place to look: no such file, ENOENT.
Call 2, [openat(AT_FDCWD, "/dev", O_WRONLY)](2): [do_open](2:do_open) The name is found, but it is a directory: it cannot be opened for writing, EISDIR.
